scenes.heading: ORC Format
scenes.subheading: Optimized columnar storage for big data
scenes.narration: ORC, the Optimized Row Columnar format, is a columnar file format built to store large volumes of data efficiently, especially in the Hadoop and Hive ecosystem.

scenes.heading: What ORC offers
bullets: Columnar layout for fast analytical reads
Built-in indexes and statistics per stripe
Strong ties to Hive and the Hadoop world
scenes.narration: ORC uses a columnar layout, so analytical queries read only the columns they need. It compresses data heavily, which greatly reduces storage costs. It embeds lightweight indexes and statistics in each stripe, letting engines skip irrelevant data. And it is tightly integrated with Hive and Hadoop, where it originated.

scenes.heading: ORC vs Parquet
scenes.narration: ORC and Parquet are both columnar formats with excellent compression and predicate push-down. ORC has especially deep roots in the Hive ecosystem, while Parquet enjoys broader support across engines like Spark and cloud warehouses. In practice, the choice often comes down to which tools your platform already favors.

scenes.text: ORC is a highly compressed columnar format that excels in Hive-based big data platforms.
scenes.narration: The essential idea is that ORC is a highly compressed columnar format that performs best within Hive-centered big data platforms.
